identity.title: A Broadband View on Microquasar MAXI J1820+070 during the 2018 Outburst

paper_type_evidence.quote: In the following, we give information about the different simultaneous observations collected from archives, covering different bands from radio to gamma-ray on April 12, 2018.

evidence.quote: The low-mass X-ray binary MAXI J$1820+070$ (=ASASSN-18ey) was first detected on 6.59 March 2018
we fix the distance of jet from the observer to the value of $d=3$ kpc

question.value: Build a quasi-simultaneous radio-to-hard-X-ray SED of MAXI J1820+070 on 12 April 2018 and model it with a leptonic jet, irradiated disk and corona

evidence.quote: Therefore we compiled quasi-simultaneous observations from public archives, Astronomer’s Telegrams, and Gamma-ray Coordination Network Circulars to construct the widest possible frequency range
we studied the spectral components independently before investigating them jointly by constructing a model consisting of a leptonic jet, an irradiated disk, and a corona
Atacama Large Millimiter/submillimiter Array (ALMA) data for project 2017.1.01103.T were retrieved from the ESO archive

analysis_steps.goal: Build the jet SED and fit a broken power law

method.value: Combine JVLA, VLITE, ALMA, X-shooter continuum and OMC points; fit radio-to-optical data with a broken power law to get the synchrotron peak and the optically thick and thin slopes, and fit the 0.3-10 GHz radio SED with a power law

evidence.quote: We fitted the radio to optical data set with a broken-power law to identify the synchrotron peak frequency and the spectral slopes of the optically thin and thick regions
For X-shooter, we considered only the part of the spectrum not affected by absorption/emission features, and averaged values for each of these intervals to obtain continuum flux density values.

key_parameters.value: Data points below 20 GHz excluded from the broken-power-law fit

evidence.quote: Similarly, we did not consider data points below 20 GHz, since they show a different slope, probably belonging to a physically distinct (and more expanded) radio jet component.

fitting.value: Levenberg-Marquardt least squares (Astropy BrokenPowerLaw1D with LevMarLSQFitter)

evidence.quote: We used the Astropy `BrokenPowerLaw1D` function (see (cite: astropy:2013; astropy:2018)) adopting the `LevMarLSQFitter` routine to perform a Levenberg-Marquardt least squares statistic.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit XMM and INTEGRAL X-ray spectra and an irradiated disk model

method.value: Fit XMM and INTEGRAL spectra with Comptonization models, a joint 0.5-400 keV fit, then a near-IR to hard X-ray fit with the diskir irradiated disk model with and without an extra power law

evidence.quote: To characterize the X-ray spectrum, a joint fit was performed between the two instruments spanning $0.5 - 400$ keV using the model `Tbabs*Reflect*(diskbb+CompTT)+Tbabs*cutoff`
Subsequently, we fit our data from the near-IR to hard X-rays using an irradiated disk model to compare with (cite: 2018ApJ...868...54S)

findings_qualitative.value: The source was in the hard state on 12 April 2018, with a flat/inverted radio spectrum and optical disk winds

evidence.quote: The flat/inverted radio spectrum and the accretion disk winds seen at optical wavelengths are also consistent with the hard state.

findings_qualitative.value: The jet is a lower limit on power because only cold protons are assumed for the hadronic content

evidence.quote: This value represents a lower limit, since we assume that the hadronic content of the jets is only in terms of cold protons, without a significant radiative contribution.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA enters as four continuum flux densities with no imaging or flux-calibration details, so the ALMA points cannot be independently checked from the paper
Abstract quotes B ~ 1.6e4 G and R ~ 2.8e9 cm while the text gives 1.8e4 G and 2.6e9 cm; the Table 4 value of B_acc in the setup list is printed as 1.8e-4 G; the VLITE flux error 5.3 is implausible
Error bars come only from MIGRAD with a frozen-parameter fit and a 5% systematic floor, so uncertainties on jet parameters are likely underestimated
Distance of 3 kpc, black hole mass of 8 solar masses and jet geometry are assumed or borrowed, and the jet luminosity scales with them
